subject.title: fix(memory): hide QMD transport metadata from recalled content

question: Should this PR merge as an adapter-only forward fix, or must memory-core also provide a one-time upgrade repair for already-persisted QMD recall snippets and derived tags before merge?
rationale: The branch correctly stops new contamination, but persistent user state already written by shipped versions remains affected; choosing whether to migrate, discard, rebuild, or intentionally leave that state requires ownership and upgrade-policy judgment.

options.title: Merge forward fix, track repair
options.body: Merge the adapter cleanup after refreshing CI, and track a separate plugin-owned doctor repair or rebuild flow for historical QMD recall records.

options.title: Require repair before merge
options.body: Hold the PR until it includes a narrowly tested memory-core migration that repairs only confidently identified QMD transport artifacts.

options.title: Accept no historical repair
options.body: Merge the adapter cleanup and explicitly document that existing short-term recall state must age out or be manually reset.

recommendation.title: Merge forward fix, track repair
recommendation.body: Merge the adapter cleanup after refreshing CI, and track a separate plugin-owned doctor repair or rebuild flow for historical QMD recall records.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged QMD work covers result metadata, MCP transport behavior, and memory-core compatibility surfaces closest to this decision.
